analyst_view.overall: Juventus are 5th with 10 points and a win would move them close to a top-eight place; Omonia (18th, 6 points) are in the play-off places but lost their last two European games. Luciano Spalletti's side beat Venezia 4-0 on Saturday, yet the injury list is long and not on the numbers' list: Kenan Yildiz (fractured foot), Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Pierre Kalulu and Kamil Grabara are out, and Kerim Alajbegovic took a shin knock on Saturday. Italian reports say Spalletti may rotate widely before the trip to Como, with Francisco Conceicao and possibly Nico Gonzalez returning. Omonia, under Henning Berg, drew 1-1 with APOEL on Saturday; Christou is injured and Magiabela doubtful. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (Juventus 2.0, Omonia 0.8) and list no absences for either side. I lean a little lower, to about 2.7, because Juventus are without Yildiz, their main creator, plus Locatelli and Thuram in midfield, and are expected to rotate before Como, although they still scored four against Venezia.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, mostly Juventus (8.0), already up for their 44 corners in the last six games. Omonia are likely to defend deep in Turin, which the split already shows, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already trimmed because Juventus draw few bookings from opponents lately (5 in six). A one-sided game with Omonia defending tends to stay calm, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, with Omonia's recent shooting already adding about 15% to their side. Rotation and the missing Yildiz should take a little off Juventus's volume, so I shade it to about 29.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, 7.6 of them for Juventus. With Yildiz out, Alajbegovic doubtful and a rotated front line likely (Woltemade and Kolo Muani as a pair, per one report), I go slightly lower, to about 9.9.
